grammar.q: Walking to school every morning [ ____ ] students a chance to wake up fully before class.
Both the size of the classroom and the number of students [ ____ ] learning.
Either the students or the teacher [ ____ ] responsible for cleaning the science lab after class.
Two-thirds of the energy used in this building [ ____ ] from solar panels on the roof.
Ten thousand won [ ____ ] not enough to buy all the materials for the art project.
The homeless in this city [ ____ ] free meals and warm clothing at the municipal shelter every evening.
The quality (of the songs on this new album) [ ____ ] surprisingly high.
The windows (in the old science room) [ ____ ] to be replaced before winter.
How you organize your notes [ ____ ] more important than how many pages you write.
Taking photos of the paintings with a flash [ ____ ] not allowed anywhere in this museum.
In the corner of the library, there [ ____ ] a few comfortable chairs for students.
Most students don’t enjoy long tests, nor [ ____ ] the teacher who has to grade them.
The key to success in many school subjects [ ____ ] regular review of what you have learned, not the number of hours you spend memorizing facts.
Players who [ ____ ] hard during the winter usually perform better in the spring, when the regular season begins and their motivation matters most.
Half of the money raised at the school festival [ ____ ] given to a local children’s hospital to cover the cost of medication for young patients.
Among the many benefits of regular exercise [ ____ ] a healthier sleep pattern during the busy exam season.
What the scientists discovered in the ancient cave [ ____ ] surprising even to the most renowned historians.
A number of recent studies [ ____ ] that regular workouts improve both memory and mood in teenagers.
The list of books recommended by the teachers [ ____ ] posted on the school website along with brief descriptions written by former students.
The paintings that the museum bought from a private collector last year [ ____ ] now on display in the newly renovated hall.
Every student and teacher in the school [ ____ ] invited to the opening ceremony of the new library.
Reading books written in a foreign language [ ____ ] students expand their vocabulary naturally.
What the students in my class want most during exam week [ ____ ] a chance to sleep a little longer.
The number of people using public transportation in the city [ ____ ] doubled since 2020, largely because of the convenience of the two new subway lines.
A number of new books about space [ ____ ] added to the school library last month.
Most of the equipment in the school’s science lab [ ____ ] donated by a local company.
Some of the cookies baked for the charity event [ ____ ] sold within an hour, and the money went to local families unable to afford heating.
There [ ____ ] a lot of evidence that sleep plays an important role in memory.
Neither the principal nor the teachers at our school [ ____ ] satisfied with the new lunch menu in the cafeteria.
Not only my parents but also my older sister [ ____ ] worried about my health during the trip.
The man who lives next to the twins in our apartment building [ ____ ] a famous physicist.
Those who [ ____ ] to join the science club should submit an application by Friday.
My sister is one of the twenty students who [ ____ ] in the school choir every week.
The news about the changes to the school schedule [ ____ ] announced this morning.
Three hours [ ____ ] too long to wait for a bus in this cold weather.
Each of the reports submitted by the students [ ____ ] to include at least three sources and a short summary of the main conclusions.
Fifty dollars [ ____ ] too much money to spend on a single concert ticket for most students.
The elderly in our neighborhood [ ____ ] invited to free health checkups at the community center.
The principal, along with several teachers, [ ____ ] invited to the education conference in Seoul.
In front of the library [ ____ ] a statue of the man who founded our school in 1950.
Both reading and writing in English [ ____ ] important skills for students who want to study abroad.
Neither my classmates nor my teacher [ ____ ] heard about the change to the exam schedule yet.
Three-quarters of the land in this region [ ____ ] covered with thick forests, which are home to many endangered species.
None of the furniture in the old house [ ____ ] damaged during the heavy storm last night.
The results of the survey conducted among teenagers in five cities [ ____ ] that most of them sleep less than seven hours.
What surprised the researchers most [ ____ ] the fact that the students’ scores improved after only two weeks.

arrange.ko: 우리 학교에서 자원봉사에 참여하는 학생 수가 매년 늘고 있다.
arrange.bogi: is increasing every year / the number of students / participating in volunteer work at our school
arrange.ans: The number of students participating in volunteer work at our school is increasing every year.

arrange.ko: 매일 아침 규칙적으로 운동하는 것은 학생들이 학교 수업에 더 잘 집중하도록 돕는다.
arrange.bogi: focus better on their classes at school / helps / exercising regularly every morning / students
arrange.ans: Exercising regularly every morning helps students focus better on their classes at school.

arrange.ko: 그 과학 동아리 회원들 중 한 명은 캐나다에서 온 교환 학생이다.
arrange.bogi: is an exchange student from Canada / of the science club / one of the members
arrange.ans: One of the members of the science club is an exchange student from Canada.

arrange.ko: 네가 매일 무엇을 먹는지가 너의 건강뿐 아니라 기분에도 영향을 준다.
arrange.bogi: affects / what / not only your health but also your mood / eat every day / you
arrange.ans: What you eat every day affects not only your health but also your mood.

arrange.ko: 같은 목표를 가진 친구들과 함께 공부하는 것은 시험 준비를 더 재미있고 덜 힘들게 만든다.
arrange.bogi: makes / more fun and less stressful / studying with friends / exam preparation / who share the same goals
arrange.ans: Studying with friends who share the same goals makes exam preparation more fun and less stressful.

arrange.ko: 십대들 사이에서 스마트폰 사용의 증가는 많은 학생들이 밤에 잠을 덜 자게 만들었다.
arrange.bogi: has led / many students / the increase in / to sleep less at night / smartphone use among teenagers
arrange.ans: The increase in smartphone use among teenagers has led many students to sleep less at night.

arrange.ko: 진정한 행복은 네가 가진 것에서가 아니라 네가 네 삶에 대해 생각하는 방식에서 온다.
arrange.bogi: not from / true happiness / how you think about your life / comes / what you have / but from
arrange.ans: True happiness comes not from what you have but from how you think about your life.

arrange.ko: 오늘날 우리가 직면한 공통의 과제들은 여러 나라의 과학자들이 함께 일하게 만들었다.
arrange.bogi: have led / the common challenges / to work together / we face today / scientists from many countries
arrange.ans: The common challenges we face today have led scientists from many countries to work together.

arrange.ko: 회사의 불법 행위를 신고하는 것은 보복에 대한 두려움 때문에 흔히 많은 용기가 필요하다.
arrange.bogi: often takes / reporting / illegal activities in a company / a lot of courage because of the fear of reprisals
arrange.ans: Reporting illegal activities in a company often takes a lot of courage because of the fear of reprisals.

translate.en: How people structure their activities and rhythms of life is largely shaped by the seven-day week.
translate.ko: 사람들이 자신의 활동과 삶의 리듬을 짜는 방식은 상당 부분 7일 단위의 일주일에 의해 형성된다.

translate.en: Fantasizing about a positive future “seduces a person to mentally enjoy the desired future in the here and now.”
translate.ko: 긍정적인 미래에 대해 환상을 품는 것은 ‘사람으로 하여금 바라는 미래를 지금 여기에서 마음속으로 즐기도록 현혹한다.’

translate.en: Positive fantasies about our future can lead us to put less effort into our goals.
translate.ko: 우리의 미래에 대한 긍정적 환상은 우리가 목표에 노력을 덜 기울이게 할 수 있다.

translate.en: Efforts like this make professionals feel like they are doing something.
translate.ko: 이와 같은 노력은 직업인들로 하여금 자신들이 무언가를 하고 있는 것처럼 느끼게 한다.

translate.en: These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize.
translate.ko: 이러한 숫자와 양식은 실제로 자연이나 인간의 어떤 본질적인 특성에 의해 좌우되는 것이 아니라, 오히려 우리가 내면화하는 사회적 창조물이다.

translate.en: Sociologists argue that our perception and usage of time are not just basic properties of nature, like a clock ticking away in the background, nor are they simply psychological phenomena of individual experience.
translate.ko: 사회학자들은 시간에 대한 우리의 인식과 사용이 배경에서 째깍거리는 시계처럼 단순히 자연의 기본 속성도 아니고, 개인 경험의 심리적 현상도 아니라고 주장한다.

translate.en: Instead, how we perceive and understand time is to a large degree shaped by tradition and cultural norms.
translate.ko: 오히려 우리가 시간을 인식하고 이해하는 방식은 상당한 정도로 전통과 문화적 기준에 의해 형성된다.

translate.en: Eviatar Zerubavel’s work, The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week , demonstrates how the week, a fundamental unit of time, is a social invention that varies across cultures, influencing how people structure their activities and rhythms of life.
translate.ko: Eviatar Zerubavel의 저서 The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week는 시간의 기본 단위인 일주일이 어떻게 사람들이 활동과 삶의 리듬을 구조화하는 방식에 영향을 끼치면서 문화마다 다른 사회적 발명품인지를 보여 준다.

translate.en: Why do we consider a nine-to-five job routine?
translate.ko: 왜 우리는 9시부터 5시까지 일하는 것을 일상으로 여기는가?

translate.en: Why don’t many of us work on the weekends?
translate.ko: 왜 우리 중 많은 사람은 주말에 일하지 않는가?

translate.en: Why do we usually pay our bills at the end of the month?
translate.ko: 왜 우리는 대개 월말에 고지 금액을 납부하는가?

translate.en: These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize and come to accept as “normal.”
translate.ko: 이러한 숫자와 양식은 실제로 자연이나 인간의 본질적인 특성에 의해 좌우되는 것이 아니라, 오히려 우리가 내면화하여 ‘정상적인 것’으로 받아들이게 된 사회적 창조물이다.

translate.en: We fall in love with the idea of a goal, pushing out of mind how different our day-to-day will need to be for us to make it happen.
translate.ko: 우리는 목표에 대한 ‘상상’과 사랑에 빠져, 그것을 실현하기 위해 우리의 하루하루가 얼마나 달라져야 할지를 생각에서 밀어낸다.
